newsitem.title: GERMANY: Palestinian sobs at 12-year sentence for hijack.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian sobs at 12-year sentence for hijack.

text.p: A German court sentenced a Palestinian woman to 12 years in jail on Tuesday for her part in the 1977 hijacking of a Lufthansa passenger jet to Somalia and the murder of its pilot.
Souhaila Andrawes, 43, is the only survivor of four Palestinians who hijacked the German airline's plane.

She broke down in tears when the presiding judge declared her guilty of murder, attempted murder and extortion. She was taken out of the courtroom to compose herself and proceedings did not recommence for 40 minutes.

Her group had hijacked the aircraft to back demands by German Red Army Faction (RAF) guerrillas for the release of 11 of its members from jail during the notorious so-called "German autumn" of left-wing extremist violence.
The prosecution asked for a 12-year sentence, rejecting Andrawes's assertion that she was not responsible for shooting the pilot as it was the gang leader who pulled the trigger.

Andrawes had already been convicted in Somalia for the hijacking and sentenced to 20 years in jail, but was released after a year and went home to Beirut. She moved to Norway in 1991 and was extradited to Germany four years later.
Early in the seven-month trial she told the court how she took up the Palestinian cause after witnessing an Israeli bombardment of a Palestinian village in the mid-1970s.
In a closing statement last week, she called the hijacking a "crass and repulsive act" which could not be justified.
Judge Albrecht Mentz said Andrawes had acted not out of base motives but to raise awareness of the Palestinian struggle. He also said she acted with "particular brutality" to the hostages.
At the time the jet was commandeered in October 1977, RAF guerrillas were holding German industrialist Hanns-Martin Schleyer hostage in a bid to get their colleagues freed.

The hijackers backed the demand and called for the release of two Palestinians jailed in Istanbul and a $15 million ransom. When their demands were not met, they shot pilot Juergen Schumann in the head during a forced stopover in Aden.
A five-day ordeal for the remaining 86 hostages ended in the Somali capital, Mogadishu, the plane's sixth stop, when West German GSG-9 commandos stormed the aircraft.
They killed all the hijackers except Andrawes, who was carried out of the plane on a stretcher making a victory sign.

Hours later, their bid for freedom foiled, three jailed members of the RAF committed suicide in their cells in Germany. One was Andreas Baader, founding member of the group which began life in 1968 as the Baader-Meinhof gang.
Schleyer was killed the same day, and his body was dumped in a car in eastern France, not far from the German border.

She will be credited with almost four years she has already spent in custody in Somalia, Norway and Germany and, after expressing regret for her actions, stands a chance of being released before her full term.
